audioLectures.title: Action Potentials & Synapses
audioLectures.transcript: In this lecture, we examine action potentials and synaptic transmission. The resting membrane potential is around minus 70 millivolts, maintained by the sodium-potassium ATPase pump which pumps three sodium ions out for every two potassium ions in. When a stimulus causes depolarization to the threshold of minus 55 millivolts, voltage-gated sodium channels open rapidly. This causes a massive influx of sodium ions and depolarization up to plus 30 millivolts. Inactivation gates close sodium channels while voltage-gated potassium channels open, allowing potassium efflux and causing repolarization, followed by a brief hyperpolarization.
audioLectures.summary:
### Core Thesis & Objective
The lecture examines the physiological mechanisms driving the action potential, specifically focusing on how the resting membrane potential is established and how sequential voltage-gated ion flux mediates depolarization, repolarization, and hyperpolarization.

---

### Key Arguments & Discussions

*   **Resting Membrane Potential (-70 mV):**
    *   Maintained by the **$\text{Na}^+/\text{K}^+$ ATPase pump**, which actively transports **3 $\text{Na}^+$ ions out** of the cell for every **2 $\text{K}^+$ ions in**.

*   **Depolarization Phase:**
    *   A stimulus must depolarize the membrane to the threshold of **-55 mV**.
    *   Reaching threshold triggers the rapid opening of **voltage-gated $\text{Na}^+$ channels**.
    *   A massive **influx of $\text{Na}^+$** drives the membrane potential up to **+30 mV**.

*   **Repolarization & Hyperpolarization Phases:**
    *   Inactivation gates close the voltage-gated $\text{Na}^+$ channels to halt $\text{Na}^+$ entry.
    *   **Voltage-gated $\text{K}^+$ channels open**, leading to a **$\text{K}^+$ efflux**.
    *   The outflow of $\text{K}^+$ causes **repolarization** of the membrane, followed by a brief period of **hyperpolarization**.

---

### Final Conclusion & Synthesis
An action potential is an all-or-none electrical event triggered when a stimulus depolarizes the resting membrane (-70 mV) to threshold (-55 mV). The precise sequence of rapid $\text{Na}^+$ influx (up to +30 mV) followed by $\text{K}^+$ efflux resets the membrane voltage through repolarization and transient hyperpolarization.
